did_you_know.text: The word “cupbearer” does not mean an ordinary waiter, but a senior court official responsible for the king’s drinks. Such a position required great trust.
The word “saris” can refer to a palace official, not necessarily to a castrated man. Here it is part of the title of two government officials.
“Captain of the guard” was probably the title of a senior commander, not a head cook. The Hebrew word is related to slaughtering.

The phrase “each according to the interpretation of his dream” emphasizes that each dream had a meaning unique to its dreamer. Thus, two dreams from the same night received completely different interpretations.
Joseph offers to interpret the dreams, but makes clear that the wisdom to do so comes from God. He presents himself as an agent, not as the source of the power.
The repetition “I was stolen, truly stolen” intensifies Joseph’s sense of injustice. It is an example of a biblical style that uses repetition for emphasis.

This is one of only two birthday celebrations explicitly described in the Bible; the other is Herod’s birthday feast in the New Testament. In both stories, the feast is connected with a fateful decision.

In the Bible, “remembering” someone can mean not only thinking of that person but also taking action for them. Thus, the cupbearer’s forgetting meant that Joseph received none of the help he had hoped for.
